title: What is Feature Engineering?
description: About transforming raw data into meaningful, informative features for machine learning.
content:
**Feature engineering** is the process of transforming raw data into a set of meaningful, informative, and non-redundant features that can be effectively used by machine learning algorithms.

The quality of features often matters as much as the choice of the model itself: even a powerful algorithm will struggle if it receives raw, messy, or uninformative inputs.

Feature engineering can be broken down into four key aspects:
• Data cleaning and preprocessing
• Feature transformation
• Feature construction
• Feature extraction

Data cleaning and preprocessing is the first step: before any transformation, the raw data often requires cleaning (e.g., handling missing values, smoothing noisy data, correcting inconsistencies). Preprocessing might include different techniques to prepare data for further transformations.

Feature transformation is needed because raw features may not directly fit the assumptions or structure required by models. This stage involves:
• Normalization
• Standardization
• Log- or power-transformation
• Encoding techniques

Feature construction is the process of creating new features by combining or aggregating existing ones. Such features can reveal hidden relationships - this step leverages domain knowledge to introduce features that might capture complex patterns more simply. For example, from a single "purchase date" column one can construct features like "day of the week" or "days since last purchase".

Feature extraction involves reducing the dimensionality of the data while retaining most of its information. Techniques such as PCA or t-SNE can automatically extract features from data. This is especially useful in visual, textual, or audial data scenarios, where the raw input (e.g., pixels or audio samples) is high-dimensional and must be compressed into a smaller set of informative features.
